licence: estimated values from the gas dispersion view/atmosphere/rayleigh.ts cites and the NIST Chemistry WebBook's density (NIST Standard Reference Data), with two measured values cited as facts; no data set is copied
reduction: n = √((1 + 2x) ÷ (1 − x)) with x = R(λ) ρ_m, the gas's molar refraction at the liquid's density, unscaled (c = 1), evaluated at each wavelength of 380–780 nm every 5 nm, to six significant figures; k = 0: the liquid is colourless in the visible. The stated band: +0.000 and −0.015 in n, the estimate likely high, as against Gagnon et al.'s values
standIn: a non-absorbing liquid whose real index is a Lorentz–Lorenz estimate from the gas's dispersion at the liquid's density, since its measured values, 1.2213 at 514.5 nm and 1.2122 at 632.8 nm at 78 K, contradict each other and lie 0.008 and 0.014 below the estimate there; at 68 K the estimate is 1.249 at 380 nm, 1.241 at 550 nm and 1.237 at 780 nm, within +0.000 and -0.015, likely high
